handwriting.notWiredTitle: Image reading is not wired up on this server
handwriting.notWiredBody: This build of the Sensei API exposes only a JSON tutor endpoint — there is no image or multipart route yet, so the photo is not sent anywhere. The tutor still receives your typed question. Once the backend adds a vision route this panel sends the image with it.

landing.tagline: Every student's personal tutor, in every language.
landing.problem: One-on-one tutoring produces the largest learning effect ever measured — Bloom's two-sigma: a tutored student outperforms 98% of their classroom peers. It has also only ever been available to families who could afford it.
landing.built: Sensei is that tutor for everyone else. It teaches Socratically — never handing over the answer, always guiding the reasoning — and it remembers you: strong in mechanics, shaky in organic chemistry, three weeks from your entrance exam. Today's lesson is built from yesterday's mistakes.
landing.p1body: Photograph your handwriting or sketch on the page. A vision model reads the script and notation and finds the exact step where you slipped.
landing.p2body: Eight languages end to end. Drop in a region's syllabus and an agent pipeline assembles the course: units, lessons, practice, mock exams.
landing.p3body: Students are minors. Their handwriting, mistakes and weak spots stay on the box — not privacy theatre, a requirement most edtech quietly violates.
landing.p4body: The whole stack runs locally on an NVIDIA DGX Spark. Unplug the network and the tutor keeps teaching.
landing.spark: Small models are fine for English chat; they fail at multilingual maths tutoring. The GB10's 128 GB of unified memory runs a 27B multilingual model locally — the difference between a toy and a tutor.
